lines.japanese: それでも学校を休むわけにはいかないのが学生の辛いところだ。
lines.english: The hard part about being a student was that, even then, you couldn't simply skip school.

lines.japanese: ああ体がだるい。俺は全身に疲労を感じつつ、机の上で伸ばした腕を枕に寝そべっていた。
lines.english: God, my body felt heavy. Exhaustion in every limb, I lay slumped across my desk with my outstretched arms for a pillow.

lines.japanese: 「聞いたよ羽田。おまえきのう、鳳凰寺カケルと遊んだらしいなァ」
lines.english: “Heard all about it, Haneda. Sounds like you spent yesterday playing with Kakeru Hououji.”

lines.japanese: まためんどくさいのがきた。俺はハリュー・クロードを見なくて済むように、横向きだった顔を机に向けた。
lines.english: Here came another nuisance. I turned my head facedown on the desk so I would not have to look at Haryu Claude.

lines.japanese: 「昨日は鬼ごっこだって？　ぷくくこりゃ残念、だったら俺も呼んでくれりゃいいのに水臭えなあ」
lines.english: “Tag, was it? Puh-kuh-kuh, shame I missed it. You should've called me. Don't be such a stranger.”

lines.japanese: 「呼んだらおまえが鳳の相手をしてくれたのか」
lines.english: “If I'd called you, would you have dealt with Otori for me?”

lines.japanese: 「はあ？　あんたらしくないねえ陛下。ニワトリなんざほっといて、どっちかが片方をボコすまで追いかけるに決まってンでしょオ」
lines.english: “Huh? That's not like you, Your Majesty. I'd ignore the chickens and chase you around till one of us beat the other to a pulp. Obviously.”

lines.japanese: 「頼むからいまここで死んでくれ」
lines.english: “Please die here and now.”

lines.japanese: 俺は机の上に伸ばした両手を中指だけ同時に立てた。
lines.english: Without lifting my hands from the desk, I raised both middle fingers at once.

lines.japanese: 「冷てえなあ」
lines.english: “Cold.”

lines.japanese: 「ひぎぃ！」
lines.english: “Hngyee!”

lines.japanese: 立てた両中指の上にハリュー・クロードの尻が落ちてきてポキリと二つの音がした。
lines.english: Haryu Claude's ass came down on my two upraised middle fingers. Two little cracks sounded.

lines.japanese: 「ぐ、ぐうっ、落ちてくるのが分かっていれば、肛門に突きたててやったものを……貴様、何故こんなむごい真似をした」
lines.english: “G-guh... Had I known you were going to descend upon me, I would have driven them into your anus... Villain, why have you done such a cruel thing?”

lines.japanese: 「八つ当たりぃ」
lines.english: “Taking it out on you.”

lines.japanese: 「そ、そんなに仲間外れにされたのが悔しかったのか」
lines.english: “W-were you really that upset about being left out?”

lines.japanese: 俺はやつの尻の下敷きになっている両手を引っこ抜きながら、孤高を持するハリュー・クロードにしては珍しい発言をされたので尋ねてみた。
lines.english: I pulled both hands out from under his ass. That was an unusually candid admission from the proudly solitary Haryu Claude, so I asked.

lines.japanese: 「ああ、残念だねェ。きのう筏なんか作ってないで演奏に行くべきだったなァ」
lines.english: “Yeah. Shame. Should've gone to perform yesterday instead of building that raft.”

lines.japanese: 「ベストチョイスだ。そのまま筏を完成させて、縦型に地球一周でもしてきてくれ」
lines.english: “Best choice you could've made. Finish the raft and take it once around the earth from pole to pole.”

lines.japanese: 珍しく饒舌にしゃべる男に視線も向けず、俺はひたすらに机に額を擦りつけた。疲れてる。早く家に帰りたい。
lines.english: Without so much as looking at the unusually talkative man, I ground my forehead against the desk. I was tired. I wanted to go home.

lines.japanese: 「おいおい陛下、元はといえばあんたが先に俺を招待したんだろ？　だったら、ン、ンンッ、今度は俺の誘いを受けるのが宮廷作法ってもんじゃないのか」
lines.english: “Now, now, Your Majesty. You're the one who invited me in the first place, remember? Then—hm, hmmm—it is only proper court etiquette that you accept my invitation in return.”

lines.japanese: ハリュー・クロードはペットボトルのキャップを捻り、ミネラルウォーターを喉に流しこんだ。
lines.english: Haryu Claude twisted the cap off a plastic bottle and poured mineral water down his throat.

lines.japanese: 「誘ってないだろバカ。おまえが勝手に暴れただけだ」
lines.english: “I never invited you, idiot. You went berserk all on your own.”

lines.japanese: 「フフフなにを言ってるんだハリボテの王様。あんたが俺をアサシンと呼んで――」
lines.english: “Hee-hee. What are you talking about, my pasteboard king? You called me an assassin, and—”

lines.japanese: 「んっ」
lines.english: “Hm.”

lines.japanese: 俺はそこでようやく顔をあげた。というよりも、ほとんど自分の意思じゃなかったかもしれない。
lines.english: Only then did I raise my face. Or perhaps it was scarcely an act of my own will.

lines.japanese: 「ん？　なんだその顔。ハリボテと言われたことが気に障ったのかい」
lines.english: “Hm? What's that look for? Did ‘pasteboard’ hurt your feelings?”

lines.japanese: 「いやそうじゃなくて、今ガード下の話をしてたんだよな？」
lines.english: “No, not that. We were talking about what happened beneath the overpass just now, weren't we?”

lines.japanese: 「あン？　ガード下ァ？」
lines.english: “Huh? Beneath the overpass?”

lines.japanese: 今度は俺がさっきのハリュー・クロードと同じ感想を持つ番だった。なんで驚いた顔してるんだ、こいつ。
lines.english: Now it was my turn to feel what Haryu Claude had a moment ago. Why did he look so surprised?

lines.japanese: 「そりゃハヤブサの話だろ。俺が言ってんのはァ、三人で遊んだときの話だよ陛下」
lines.english: “That was Hayabusa. I'm talking about when the three of us played together, Your Majesty.”

lines.japanese: なんだ、なんのことを言ってるんだこいつ。俺はなんとか理解を努めようと、小首を傾げて考えてみた。
lines.english: What? What was he talking about? I cocked my head and tried to work it out.

lines.japanese: だが先に理解出来たのは自分の状態だった。頭を横に傾けてみてようやく分かったことだが、耳からなにか垂れおちてるじゃないか。
lines.english: But the first thing I managed to understand was my own condition. Only when I tilted my head did I realize something was running out of my ear.

lines.japanese: 「おわあっ」
lines.english: “Waaah!”

lines.japanese: 慌ててこぼれたものを掴んで耳の中に突っこんだ。それじゃ足りないと思って、口からも飲みこんだ。
lines.english: I frantically caught what had spilled and shoved it back into my ear. Afraid that would not be enough, I swallowed some through my mouth as well.

lines.japanese: 「……なんだぁ、ソレ」
lines.english: “...What the hell is that?”

lines.japanese: 「な、なんでもない。それより思いだしたぞ、さんざっぱらストンピングを浴びせてくれたときだな。てめえ無抵抗の亀を捕まえた挙句ふざけた真似をしやがって」
lines.english: “N-nothing. More important, I remember now. When you stomped the hell out of me. You caught a helpless turtle and then pulled that shit.”

lines.japanese: 「はぁ、俺にゃ見えないけどなんかそこにあんのかい。だったらもっと飲みこんどけよ。大事なモンまで零したら困るでしょう」
lines.english: “Huh. Can't see it myself, but is there something there? Better swallow some more. Wouldn't want anything important spilling out.”

lines.japanese: ハリュー・クロードが机の上の何かを掴み、俺の口の中めがけて突っこんだ。
lines.english: Haryu Claude picked up something from the desk and thrust it toward my mouth.

lines.japanese: 一度に多くの記憶を回収したせいか、画面が真っ白になった。
lines.english: Perhaps I recovered too many memories at once. The screen went white.

lines.japanese: 団地。学校。ユキ姉。お母さん。
lines.english: The housing project. School. Yuki. Mom.

lines.japanese: プラモ。肉じゃが。近所のスーパー。お母さん。やめてよお母さん。無機質なグレーの壁。お母さん。
lines.english: Model kits. Meat and potatoes. The neighborhood supermarket. Mom. Stop it, Mom. Featureless gray walls. Mom.

lines.japanese: 優しかったじいさん。６年生のゼッケン。フリッキー５のポスター。ブッ殺すぞコノヤロウ。小鳩。パルクレープ。アレキサンダー。美空学園。
lines.english: The kind old man. My sixth-grade number bib. A Fricky Five poster. I'll fucking kill you, asshole. Kobato. Paru Crêpes. Alexander. Misora Academy.

lines.japanese: あれ、今どこだ。そうだ美空学園じゃん。
lines.english: Wait. Where was I now? Right. Misora Academy.

lines.japanese: 俺は何度か首を振って今の状況を確認した。なんのこともない。いつもと変わらない教室だ。
lines.english: I shook my head several times and checked my surroundings. Nothing unusual. The same old classroom.

lines.japanese: そのとき俺を観察するような視線に気がついた。普段は回遊魚みたいにさ迷っている目が薄ら笑いの中で俺を見ている。
lines.english: Then I noticed someone studying me. Eyes that usually roved in endless circles like migratory fish were watching me now through the curve of a faint smile.

lines.japanese: 「どうした羽田」
lines.english: “What's wrong, Haneda?”

lines.japanese: 「別に」
lines.english: “Nothing.”

lines.japanese: 俺は席を立ってやつを置きざりにしてやった。こういう構ってちゃんは相手にしないでやるのが一番効果的だ。
lines.english: I got up and left him there. The best way to deal with an attention seeker like him was to deny him any attention at all.

lines.japanese: その後は放課後になるまで大人しく一日を過ごした。体は疲れていたがこのまま帰る気にはなれず、学校が終わったらアルバイトに向かうことにした。
lines.english: After that, I passed the day quietly until school ended. My body was tired, but I didn't feel like going straight home, so once classes were over, I headed to my part-time job.

lines.japanese: 「おはようございまーっす」
lines.english: “Good morning!”

lines.japanese: 「はい。おはようございます」
lines.english: “Good morning.”

lines.japanese: 制服から私服に着替えていたらギリギリの時間になってしまった。同じ時間に学校は終わってるはずなのに、とっくに着替え終わってる玉泉。
lines.english: Changing out of my school uniform had left me cutting it close. Her school should have let out at the same time as mine, yet Tamaizumi had long since finished changing.

lines.japanese: 「いや遅くなってすまん。すぐ着替えてくる」
lines.english: “Sorry I'm late. I'll get changed right away.”

lines.japanese: 「はあ。別にまだ始業時間じゃありませんから、ゆっくりでも構いませんよ」
lines.english: “Oh. Your shift hasn't started yet, so you may take your time.”

lines.japanese: もう少しソフトな表情で言ってくれてもいいのに、淡々と事務的に語る玉泉。ああこいつはいつだって同じ態度だから安心できるなあ。
lines.english: She could have said it with a slightly gentler expression, but Tamaizumi delivered it with her usual dry efficiency. Ahh. She was always exactly the same. How reassuring.

lines.japanese: 「な、なんですかその陶酔したような顔は」
lines.english: “Wh-what is that rapturous look for?”

lines.japanese: 「えっ、俺がハンサム？」
lines.english: “What? You think I'm handsome?”

lines.japanese: 玉泉はメモ帳を手にとってなにか言いたげに俺を見つめた。
lines.english: Tamaizumi picked up a notepad and looked at me as though she had something to say.

lines.japanese: 「いや中耳炎とかじゃないから、そんな真面目に筆談の心配をするな」
lines.english: “I don't have an ear infection. Don't start seriously worrying that we'll have to communicate in writing.”

lines.japanese: 「はあ」
lines.english: “I see.”

lines.japanese: 「なんかおまえ、行動が渡来に似てきたな」
lines.english: “You're starting to act a lot like Watarai.”

lines.japanese: 「はい」
lines.english: “Yes.”

lines.japanese: 「なんだと」
lines.english: “What did you say?”

lines.japanese: 時間がないので相手にするのはやめておいた。
lines.english: I had no time, so I chose not to engage.

lines.japanese: さあ今日も一日がんばるぞっ。
lines.english: All right. Let's give it our best today too!

lines.japanese: 「ねー、えりちゃんも一緒にクリスマスパーティーしようよう。私、友達に誘われてるんさ」
lines.english: “Come on, Eri, have a Christmas party with us! My friend invited me.”

lines.japanese: で、一時間後にはこのひとに元気よく声をかけられた。まあいつものことだからいいんだけど。
lines.english: An hour later, this woman was already calling out to me at full strength. Well, it happened every day, so fine.

lines.japanese: 「誘われてるって、紀奈子さん受験生じゃないですか。いいんですか、この時期にそんなことしてて」
lines.english: “Invited you? Kinako, you're preparing for your entrance exams. Should you really be doing that at this time of year?”

lines.japanese: 「たまには息抜きも必要だよう。普段はちゃんとやってるからいいんだい」
lines.english: “Everybody needs a break now and then. I study properly the rest of the time, so it's fine.”

lines.japanese: 「え、たまには……？　普段？」
lines.english: “Now and then...? The rest of the time?”

lines.japanese: 「そうだ二人でプレゼント買いに行こうよ。なんだか学生のころみたいでわくわくするね」
lines.english: “Oh, I know! Let's go buy presents together. It'll be exciting, just like when we were students.”

lines.japanese: 「紀奈子さん、ソレ全然たまじゃないですよ。すんごく童心に帰ってますよ。受験なんて忘れる気満々じゃないすか」
lines.english: “Kinako, this is way beyond once in a while. You've completely regressed to childhood. You're plainly planning to forget those exams exist.”

lines.japanese: 「そ、そんなことないよーう！　ねえねえじゃあ一日だけでいいから付きあってよー」
lines.english: “Th-that's not true! Come on, come with me for just one day!”

lines.japanese: 「あーもー……まあ楽しそうだから行くには行くけど」
lines.english: “Oh, fine... It sounds fun, so I'll go.”

lines.japanese: 「つーかヒノエリ、クリスマスなのに予定ないんだ」
lines.english: “Wait, Hinoeri. You don't have plans for Christmas?”

lines.japanese: 「やだぁ、カケルったら私が浮気しないか心配ばっかりするんだからぁ」
lines.english: “Oh, Kakeru, you spend all your time worrying I might cheat on you.”

lines.japanese: 「死ねよ腐れマ×コ」
lines.english: “Die, you rotten c×nt.”

lines.japanese: 「まぁでも予定ならこうやって上手いこと入るもんだよね。もしかしたら紀奈子さんのパーティーにすんーげかっこいい子が来るかもしれないじゃん」
lines.english: “But that's how plans work out, isn't it? Maybe somebody incredibly hot will show up at Kinako's party.”

lines.japanese: 「いやあんた、なに先輩の誘いにまでがっついてんすか」
lines.english: “Seriously? You're even using your senior's invitation to hunt for men?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、全員女の子だよ」
lines.english: “Oh, it's all girls.”

lines.japanese: 「えー」
lines.english: “Aww.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、半ば冗談で言ってるのかと思ってたら、本気でがっついてたんだ」
lines.english: “Oh. I thought you were at least half joking, but you really were hunting.”

lines.japanese: 「鳳君も来る？」
lines.english: “Would you like to come too, Otori?”

lines.japanese: 「行くわけねーだろバーカ」
lines.english: “Like hell, idiot.”

lines.japanese: 「行くわけないってことは、予定があるんじゃないんだ。なぁ～んだ、カケルもうちらと一緒じゃん」
lines.english: “If you aren't going, that means you don't have other plans. Aww, Kakeru, you're just like us.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ俺、前日まで選択権あるから」
lines.english: “I've got the right to choose until the day before.”

lines.japanese: 「ヒエラルキーの最上階！」
lines.english: “The very top floor of the social hierarchy!”

lines.japanese: 「ああそうそう、凄いマンションの上の方の階なんだって。眺めが凄くいいらしいよ」
lines.english: “Oh, yes. It's on one of the upper floors of an incredible apartment building. Apparently the view is wonderful.”

lines.japanese: 「そりゃ凄いっすねえ。一度そういうとこ住んでみたかったし、ちょっと楽しみになってきたかも」
lines.english: “That does sound amazing. I've always wanted to live somewhere like that. Maybe I'm getting a little excited.”

lines.japanese: 「うんじゃあえりちゃんも一緒に行こうね」
lines.english: “Then you'll come with me, Eri.”

lines.japanese: うん、と目を合わせて紀奈子さんと英里子さんが頷いた。なんとなく和らいだ空気の中、コーヒーを口に含んだカケルくんが、カップをソーサーにことりと乗せる。
lines.english: Kinako and Eriko met each other's eyes and nodded. In the softened atmosphere, Kakeru took a sip of coffee and set the cup down on its saucer with a quiet click.

lines.japanese: 「で、何時に行けばいいの」
lines.english: “So, what time should I be there?”

lines.japanese: 「行くんだ！」
lines.english: “You are going!”

lines.japanese: 相変わらず難しい精神構造だなあ。でも水を差してもなんだし、なにも言わないでおくことにした。
lines.english: His mind remained as difficult to understand as ever. But there was no point spoiling the mood, so I kept quiet.

lines.japanese: 「で、千歳君の予定は？」
lines.english: “And what are your plans, Chitose?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、俺ですか？　俺は――」
lines.english: “Oh, me? I'm—”

lines.japanese: 「千歳さん、またお話してるんですか」
lines.english: “Chitose, are you chatting again?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、玉泉」
lines.english: “Oh. Tamaizumi.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、ひよちゃーん！　ねえねえ、ひよちゃんはクリスマスどんな予定だい？」
lines.english: “Oh, Hiyooo! Hey, Hiyo, what are your plans for Christmas?”

lines.japanese: 「は？　はあ、普通に家族と過ごすと思いますが」
lines.english: “What? Oh... I expect I'll spend it with my family as usual.”

lines.japanese: 「ふーん、寂しいクリスマスだねえ」
lines.english: “Hmm. Sounds like a lonely Christmas.”

lines.japanese: 「あんたが言うのか」
lines.english: “You're one to talk.”

lines.japanese: 「ふーん。ねえひよちゃん、一緒にクリスマスパーティーやらない？」
lines.english: “Hmm. Hey, Hiyo, want to come to a Christmas party with us?”

lines.japanese: 「えっ、だって紀奈子さん、受験生じゃないですか」
lines.english: “But Kinako, aren't you studying for your entrance exams?”

lines.japanese: 「えー、だって息抜きも必要だよう」
lines.english: “What? Everybody needs a break.”

lines.japanese: 「そのやり取りはワンセットやったからもういい」
lines.english: “We've already performed that entire routine once. No encore.”

lines.japanese: 「はあ。それより千歳さん、業務中に私語は……」
lines.english: “I see. More to the point, Chitose, private conversation while you're working—”

lines.japanese: 「はー？　なにそれ私にも言ってんの？」
lines.english: “Huh? Is that supposed to be aimed at me too?”

lines.japanese: 「いえ……そういうつもりでは……」
lines.english: “No... That wasn't my intention...”

lines.japanese: 「ああいやいや！　俺もそろそろ真面目にやろうかなと思ってたとこだった。あ、ほらほらちょうどお客さんも来たみたいだし！」
lines.english: “No, no! I was just thinking it was time I started working seriously. Oh, look! I think a customer just came in!”

lines.japanese: 「ちぇー。じゃあ紀奈子さん、また後でね」
lines.english: “Tch. All right, Kinako. See you later.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、みんなも暇が出来たら話しかけてねー」
lines.english: “Okay. The rest of you come talk to me when you get a free minute too!”

lines.japanese: 英里子さんは仕事に戻っていった。紀奈子さんもカケルくんとなにか話しはじめたみたいだ。
lines.english: Eriko returned to work. Kinako appeared to have started talking with Kakeru about something.

lines.japanese: 玉泉の言う通り遊びすぎてたし、いっちょ真面目にやるか。
lines.english: Tamaizumi was right: I'd been fooling around too much. Time to get serious.

lines.japanese: 「いらっしゃいませ……」
lines.english: “Welcome...”

lines.japanese: 「あれっ、米田さん」
lines.english: “Oh. Yoneda.”

lines.japanese: と思ったら、またしても知り合いだった。
lines.english: Only to discover, once again, that the customer was somebody I knew.

lines.japanese: 「やっ、千歳君。コスプレしてるくせに、最近編集部の方は顔出さないじゃん」
lines.english: “Hey, Chitose. You'll cosplay as a waiter here, but you haven't shown your face around the editorial office lately.”

lines.japanese: 「出さないっていうか、そりゃ用もないのに遊びにいくわけにはいかないですよ」
lines.english: “It's not that I won't show my face. I can't exactly drop by to play when I don't have any business there.”

lines.japanese: 「たまには自分から売りこみに来ないと、忘れちゃうかもしれないよ？　私だって忙しいんだから」
lines.english: “If you don't come sell yourself once in a while, I might forget about you. I'm busy too, you know.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、まあそう……ですよねえ。ははは」
lines.english: “Ah, well, yes... That's true. Hahaha.”

lines.japanese: つってもその忙しさを知ってるからこそ、俺のことで時間を割かせられないと思っちゃうんだけどね。
lines.english: But knowing how busy she was was exactly what made me feel I shouldn't ask her to spend time on me.

lines.japanese: 「ま、そんな消極的な千歳君に、いい仕事があるんだ。引きうけてくれない？」
lines.english: “Well, I happen to have a good job for such a passive young man. Would you take it?”

lines.japanese: 「え、俺に？」
lines.english: “What, for me?”

lines.japanese: 米田さんは席にも着かずに鞄の中をごそごそと探りはじめた。まさかそのために来たんじゃないだろうけど、わざわざ俺に振ってくれるなんてありがたいなあ。
lines.english: Without even taking a seat, Yoneda began rummaging through her bag. Surely she hadn't come here just for that, but I was grateful she had gone out of her way to offer the work to me.

lines.japanese: 俺を評価してくれている米田さんにちょっぴり感謝した。
lines.english: I felt a little surge of gratitude toward Yoneda for thinking so highly of me.

lines.japanese: 「今回のは千歳君にぴったりの仕事なんだけど、実は――」
lines.english: “This job is perfect for you, Chitose. The thing is—”

lines.japanese: 「千歳さん」
lines.english: “Chitose.”

lines.japanese: が、そこに教官様の登場。さっき怒られたばっかりなのによくないな。
lines.english: And there stood my drill instructor. She had only just scolded me. This wasn't good.

lines.japanese: 「あ、す、すいません、ちょっと知り合いだったから……」
lines.english: “Oh, s-sorry. She's someone I know, so...”

lines.japanese: 「あの、せめて席へお通ししてからにしてください。ここではお客様の目にも留まります」
lines.english: “At least show her to a table first. Standing here makes you conspicuous to the other customers.”

lines.japanese: 「ああゴメンね私のせいで……おっ？」
lines.english: “Oh, sorry. My fault... Oh?”

lines.japanese: 米田さんは顔だけ上げて日和子さんに謝ろうとしたが、何かを思いだしたように玉泉の顔をじっと見つめた。
lines.english: Yoneda lifted her head to apologize to Hiyoko, but then stared at Tamaizumi's face as if something had come back to her.

lines.japanese: 「えっ？」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 「キミはえっと……細川タマちゃんだ」
lines.english: “You're... Tama Hosokawa.”

lines.japanese: 「え、ええっ？」
lines.english: “Wh-what?”

lines.japanese: 「覚えてないかな。私、前に駅で会ったことあるんだけど」
lines.english: “Don't you remember me? We met at the station once before.”

lines.japanese: げっ。嫌なことを思いだすなぁ。鷲介が玉泉日和子と初めて会った日じゃないか。
lines.english: Ghk. Don't remind me of that. That was the day Shusuke first met Hiyoko Tamaizumi.

lines.japanese: 「あ、ああ、あのときの……」
lines.english: “Oh. Oh, you were the woman from...”

lines.japanese: 「うちの作家さんだったとは気づかなくて――ああゴメン、私、祥玄社の編集で『メンズフリーズ』って雑誌なんかを担当してる米田です」
lines.english: “I didn't realize you were one of our authors—oh, sorry. I'm Yoneda, an editor at Shogensha. I work on a magazine called *Men's Freeze*, among other things.”

lines.japanese: 「祥玄社の……あっ、い、いつもお世話になっております！　す、すみません、こんな所でっ、やだ、私なんて格好っ……」
lines.english: “Shogensha... Oh! Th-thank you for everything! I'm sorry to meet you somewhere like this. Oh no, dressed like this...”

lines.japanese: 「分かってると思いますけど動揺してます」
lines.english: “As I'm sure you can tell, she's flustered.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、そうみたいだね。あの、大丈夫だよ。祥玄社の編集って言っても私は文庫の方とは別の部署だから」
lines.english: “Yes, I gathered. Don't worry. I may be an editor at Shogensha, but I work in a different department from the paperback division.”

lines.japanese: 「そ、そうでしたか」
lines.english: “O-oh. I see.”

lines.japanese: ああそうか。俺、知らないことになってるから言えないけど、玉泉は三作目を持ちこんで気持ちがデリケートな状態なんだな。
lines.english: Ah, of course. I wasn't supposed to know, so I couldn't say it aloud, but Tamaizumi was in a delicate emotional state after submitting her third book.

lines.japanese: 「あ、でもいい機会だから挨拶しておかなくちゃね。今度うちの雑誌に『ほほえみインサイド』の紹介文を掲載いたしますのでよろしくお願いします」
lines.english: “Oh, and this is a good chance to introduce myself. We’ll be running a piece on *Smile Inside* in our magazine soon. I look forward to working with you.”
“What... Excuse me?”

lines.japanese: 「ぶっ」
lines.english: “Pfft!”

lines.japanese: 本人を目の前にしてなんてこと言いだしやがりますかこの女は。俺はあわあわとした様子を手の動きで表した。
lines.english: What the hell are you telling her that for when she's standing right here, woman? I flapped my hands in panic.

lines.japanese: 「はあ……千歳さんからも挨拶はしていただきました」
lines.english: “I see... Chitose has already introduced himself to me as well.”

lines.japanese: 「そうそう、千歳君が精魂込めて書いてくれたお陰で、いい記事になってます。ご期待ください」
lines.english: “Yes, exactly. Thanks to all the heart and soul Chitose poured into it, the article turned out wonderfully. I hope you'll look forward to it.”

lines.japanese: うひぃ、やめてえ。俺は授業参観で母への手紙を読まれた小学生みたく、身を小さくしながら羞恥プレイに悶えた。
lines.english: Eeeugh, stop! Like an elementary-school boy hearing his letter to his mother read aloud at parents' day, I shrank into myself and writhed in mortification.
“...Excuse me.”

lines.japanese: 「は、はい」
lines.english: “Y-yes?”

lines.japanese: そして日和子さんからのお言葉。
lines.english: And now, a word from Hiyoko.

lines.japanese: 「千歳さん、小休憩に入っていいですよ」
lines.english: “Chitose, you may take a short break.”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 「中途半端にやられるよりは区切りをつけてもらった方がいいですし」
lines.english: “It would be better to let you finish this properly than have you work with your attention divided.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、そ、そう……なの？」
lines.english: “Oh. R-really...?”

lines.japanese: 「はい、１５分程度なら。私が店長に許可を取っておきます」
lines.english: “Yes. About fifteen minutes. I'll ask the manager for permission.”

lines.japanese: 「えっと……はあ」
lines.english: “Um... Okay.”

lines.japanese: これじゃ。でもあの玉泉が、例え１５分とはいえ融通を利かせてくれるとは……。
lines.english: Well, this was awkward. Still, Tamaizumi of all people was making an accommodation for me, even if it was only fifteen minutes...

lines.japanese: 「必要ありませんか？」
lines.english: “Do you not need it?”

lines.japanese: 「あっ、いやいや助かる。さんきゅー玉泉」
lines.english: “Oh! No, no, it helps. Thanks, Tamaizumi.”

lines.japanese: 玉泉はすぐにマスターの元に向かっていった。うーん、あれはやっぱり、喜んでくれた……んだろうなあ。
lines.english: Tamaizumi went straight over to the manager. Hmm. That meant she really was... pleased, didn't it?

lines.japanese: 改めて、玉泉の三作目が編集さんに読んでもらえるといいなあと思う。米田さんを席に案内しながらそんなことを考えた。
lines.english: Once again, I found myself hoping an editor would read Tamaizumi's third book. I thought about it as I showed Yoneda to a table.

lines.japanese: 「で、千歳君にお願いしたい仕事なんだけど、この前うちの紹介記事でアイドルもの書いてもらったでしょ」
lines.english: “So, about the job I'd like you to do. You wrote that idol piece for one of our features, remember?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、ありましたね。そんなに好評でしたか」
lines.english: “Oh, yes. Was it that well received?”

lines.japanese: 「うん、その号はまだ発売されてないからいいんだけど、今度フリッキー５がベスト盤出したんでしょ？　別の雑誌で似たような特集組むらしいのよ」
lines.english: “Well, the issue isn't out yet, but Fricky Five just released a greatest-hits album, right? Another magazine is apparently putting together a similar feature.”

lines.japanese: 「で、まだライター決まってなかったからさ。いいやついるんすよって言って、勝手に仕事もらっちゃった」
lines.english: “They hadn't chosen a writer yet, so I told them I knew a good one and accepted the job for you without asking.”

lines.japanese: 「え、マジすか。俺ってそんなに米田評価高かったんだ」
lines.english: “Seriously? I didn't know I rated that highly on the Yoneda scale.”

lines.japanese: 「で、どう？　やってくれる？」
lines.english: “So? Will you do it?”

lines.japanese: 「もちろんでしょう。そこまで信頼してもらってるのに、断るわけにいかないじゃないすか」
lines.english: “Of course. If you trust me that much, how could I possibly turn you down?”

lines.japanese: 「うん、私はあの記事、まだ全部読んでないんだけどね」
lines.english: “Sure. Though I still haven't finished reading that other article.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ、あれから結構時間たってるのにまだ読んでくれてないんですか。酷いなあ、ちゃんと穴という穴が開くまで読んでくださいよ」
lines.english: “What? It's been ages, and you still haven't read it? That's awful. Read it properly—read it until you've worn holes clean through it.”

lines.japanese: 「だっていざ読んでみてがっかりする結果だったら、新しいライター探さなくちゃいけないでしょ。ね、真実は時として知らない方がいいこともあるんだよ」
lines.english: “But if I finally read it and discover it's disappointing, I'll have to find a new writer. Sometimes the truth is better left unknown.”

lines.japanese: 「記事も鳴かずば撃たれまい！」
lines.english: “Had the article kept its mouth shut, it would never have been shot!”

lines.japanese: 「あはは、じゃあ今からどんなもの書いてもらうか説明するけどいい？」
lines.english: “Ahaha. Shall I explain what I want you to write, then?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、はいはい」
lines.english: “Oh. Sure, sure.”

lines.japanese: 俺はポケットに忍びこませていたメモ帳とシャーペンを取りだした。
lines.english: I took the notepad and mechanical pencil I kept concealed in my pocket.

lines.japanese: 「ご注文お待たせしました」
lines.english: “Thank you for waiting.”

lines.japanese: と思ったら、その前に日和子さんがアイスティーを運んできてくれた。俺と米田さんの前に一つずつ。
lines.english: Before we could begin, Hiyoko brought us iced tea. One glass in front of Yoneda and one in front of me.

lines.japanese: ん、一つずつ？　俺、注文した覚えないぞ。
lines.english: Hm? One each? I didn't remember ordering anything.

lines.japanese: 「ではごゆっくり」
lines.english: “Please take your time.”

lines.japanese: 「おい玉泉、これ……」
lines.english: “Hey, Tamaizumi, this...”

lines.japanese: 「はあ。お話するなら飲み物があった方がいいでしょう」
lines.english: “Well, if you're going to talk, it would be better to have something to drink.”

lines.japanese: 「え、これくれるの？」
lines.english: “You're giving this to me?”

lines.japanese: 玉泉は無言で頷いた。うーん、優しいなあ今日の玉泉……顔はまるで笑ってないけど。
lines.english: Tamaizumi nodded in silence. She was awfully kind today... Her face wasn't smiling in the slightest, though.

lines.japanese: 「はは、ありがとな玉泉。後半は真面目にやるから」
lines.english: “Hah. Thanks, Tamaizumi. I'll work seriously in the second half.”

lines.japanese: 「はあ。期待しています」
lines.english: “I see. I look forward to it.”

lines.japanese: まるで期待なんかしちゃいないと言った顔で玉泉は立ち去った。
lines.english: Tamaizumi walked away with a face that said she looked forward to nothing of the sort.

lines.japanese: 「じゃ、仕事の話に戻るけど、これが最近出たフリッキー５のベスト盤ね」
lines.english: “Back to business. This is the Fricky Five greatest-hits album that came out recently.”

lines.japanese: 「ああこれなら俺、持ってますよ」
lines.english: “Oh, I've already got this one.”

lines.japanese: 「へー、じゃあ説明の必要はないかな。このＣＤも要らない？」
lines.english: “Really? Then I suppose you don't need an explanation. Don't need this CD either?”

lines.japanese: 「いえ、千歳さんが必要なくても店内で使います」
lines.english: “No. Even if Chitose doesn't need it, we can use it in the café.”

lines.japanese: 「うわあ」
lines.english: “Whoa.”

lines.japanese: 居なくなったと思った玉泉が隣に座っていた。しかも仕事の話に割りこんできた。
lines.english: Tamaizumi, whom I thought had left, was sitting beside us. Worse, she had joined the business discussion.

lines.japanese: 「ていうかおまえ仕事……」
lines.english: “Wait, aren't you supposed to be working...?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、店長すみません、小休憩に入ります」
lines.english: “Oh. Manager, excuse me. I'm taking a short break.”

lines.japanese: 「玉泉が堕ちた！」
lines.english: “Tamaizumi has fallen from grace!”

lines.japanese: しかし玉泉は俺のツッコミなど意にも介さず、ＣＤのジャケットを近づけたり遠ざけたりして眺めていた。
lines.english: But Tamaizumi paid my retort no mind. She studied the CD cover, bringing it close to her face, then holding it at arm's length.

lines.japanese: 「ていうか店内でかけられるかなあ……」
lines.english: “Can we even play that in here...?”

lines.japanese: 「それは分かりませんが、せっかくあるなら使いましょう」
lines.english: “I don't know. But since it's available, we may as well use it.”

lines.japanese: 「俺の仕事用だ」
lines.english: “It's for my job.”

lines.japanese: 「だって千歳さんは持ってるって言いましたよね？　だったらせっかく貸していただけるものを使わないと勿体ないじゃないですか」
lines.english: “You just said you already own it, didn't you? In that case, it would be wasteful not to use the copy she was kind enough to lend us.”

lines.japanese: 「お、おまえなあ……」
lines.english: “Y-you...”

lines.japanese: 「あー、いいよいいよ持ってって。どうせ私は聞かないんだし」
lines.english: “Oh, it's fine. Go ahead and take it. I wasn't going to listen to it anyway.”

lines.japanese: 「どうしてですか、ちゃんと聞いてください」
lines.english: “Why not? You should listen to it properly.”

lines.japanese: 「ええー」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 「そうですよ米田さん、フリッキーはいま聞いてもいいですよ？」
lines.english: “She's right, Yoneda. Fricky still holds up today.”

lines.japanese: 「なんなのこの子たちー」
lines.english: “What is with you two?”

lines.japanese: 「この前列右が細川くん、通称ホソリューです。そしてこの後列右にいるのが京極涼彦、通称殿下です」
lines.english: “The one on the right in the front row is Hosokawa, known as Hosoryu. And the one on the right in the back row is Suzuhiko Kyogoku, known as His Highness.”

lines.japanese: 「ヤケに詳しいな玉泉」
lines.english: “You know an awful lot about this, Tamaizumi.”

lines.japanese: 「い、いえ、私は紹介記事を書いていただいたお礼に、千歳さんの手助けが出来ればと思って……」
lines.english: “N-no. I merely thought I might help you in return for writing that article...”

lines.japanese: 「そ、そうだったのか。すまない、そんな風に考えてくれていたのに、楽しんでるなあこのひととか思っちゃって……」
lines.english: “O-oh. I see. Sorry. Here you were thinking so kindly of me, and I assumed you were enjoying yourself...”

lines.japanese: 「んー、私はやっぱりホソリューが好きかなあ」
lines.english: “Hmm. I suppose Hosoryu is still my favorite.”

lines.japanese: 「ですよね！」
lines.english: “Exactly!”

lines.japanese: 楽しんでるなあこのひと。まあいいけど。
lines.english: She was enjoying herself. Well, fine.

lines.japanese: 「ま、のぶちんも好きだったけどね。あと仲がよかったから、マサシも気に入ってたな。二人でバラエティにも出てたしさ」
lines.english: “I liked Nobuchin too. And since they were close, I had a soft spot for Masashi. Those two used to appear on variety shows together.”

lines.japanese: 「ふーん、結構いいところ突いてきますね」
lines.english: “Hmm. You have surprisingly good taste.”

lines.japanese: 「おーい、さっきから全然話に出てこないんだけど、ヨッくんはどうした」
lines.english: “Hey, you've talked about everybody else. What about Yoshi?”

lines.japanese: 「ヨッくんはちょっとねえ……」
lines.english: “Yoshi is a little...”

lines.japanese: 「なんで！　なんで他のメンバーの話をして、ヨッくんだけは避けようとするんだおまえら！」
lines.english: “Why?! Why do both of you talk about every other member, then deliberately avoid Yoshi?!”

lines.japanese: 「ヨッくんいい。だって彼スキャンダル起こしてたじゃないですか。それよりも綺麗な体のホソリューがいいんです」
lines.english: “Yoshi is out. He had that scandal, remember? I'd much rather have the spotless Hosoryu.”

lines.japanese: 「あったねー、足利芳樹ストーカー事件。私もあれでのぶちんに乗りかえたなあ」
lines.english: “Oh, yes—the Yoshiki Ashikaga Stalker Incident. That's when I switched to Nobuchin too.”

lines.japanese: 「くっ、そんなに綺麗な体が好きなら二次元の世界にでも浸ってろい。いいよふんだ、職権濫用してヨッくんのこと褒めちぎってやるんだい」
lines.english: “Ghk. If spotless men are all you want, go lose yourselves in fictional heartthrobs. Fine! Hmph! I'll abuse my professional authority and fill the whole thing with praise for Yoshi!”

lines.japanese: 「こーら、仕事は真面目にやりなさい」
lines.english: “Hey, now. Take the job seriously.”

lines.japanese: 「いやね、脇がしっかりと固まっているからこそ主役が光るんですよ。ホソリューなんて黙ってても人気が出るキャラなんか、三行にまとめてやるもんね」
lines.english: “Listen, a star only shines because the supporting cast is solid. A guy like Hosoryu would be popular without any help, so I'll sum him up in three lines.”

lines.japanese: 「うわ、最低……」
lines.english: “Wow. You're awful...”

lines.japanese: 「んっ、なんだなんだ俺の話か？」
lines.english: “Hm? What's this? Talking about me?”

lines.japanese: 「自他共に認める最低きちゃったー」
lines.english: “And here comes the worst guy alive. He’ll even tell you so himself.”

lines.japanese: マスターは突然やってきて、何のためらいもなく、俺たちが囲むテーブルの椅子を引いてどっかと腰を下ろした。
lines.english: The manager appeared from nowhere, pulled out a chair at our table without the slightest hesitation, and planted himself in it.

lines.japanese: 「おう、優！　久しぶりだな、一緒に避妊しよう！」
lines.english: “Hey, Yu! Long time no see. Let's use contraception together!”

lines.japanese: 「おっしゃるとおり最低ですね」
lines.english: “You are every bit as awful as advertised.”

lines.japanese: 「なるほど、生がよかったのか」
lines.english: “Ah. You wanted it raw.”

lines.japanese: 「紛れもなく最低ですね」
lines.english: “You are indisputably awful.”

lines.japanese: 「ところで玉泉君、俺と二人で避妊しないか」
lines.english: “By the way, Tamaizumi, would you like to use contraception alone with me?”

lines.japanese: 「あんたそれしかないのか！」
lines.english: “Is that all you've got?!”

lines.japanese: 「ふふふ、左手の枷を外し、自由の翼を手に入れた俺にもはや怖いものなどないのだ。『洗練された伊達』ことこの狩男が牙を生やしてナイト・ブレイク・メイク・アーップ！　さあ飛びこんでこい玉泉君！」
lines.english: “Heh-heh-heh. I have cast off the shackle on my left hand and claimed the wings of freedom. Now nothing can frighten me. I, Karuo, called the Sophisticated Dandy, bare my fangs and—Night Break Make Up! Come, Tamaizumi! Fly into my arms!”

lines.japanese: 「店長。私、仕事に戻ります」
lines.english: “Manager. I'm going back to work.”

lines.japanese: 玉泉はガタンと席を立ち、さっさと下の階に向かってしまった。
lines.english: Tamaizumi shoved back her chair with a clatter and promptly headed downstairs.

lines.japanese: 「あーあ、怒らせちゃった」
lines.english: “Oh, dear. You made her angry.”

lines.japanese: 「ふふふ、かわいいやつめ。俺のために仕事をしてくれるのか」
lines.english: “Heh-heh. What a sweet girl. Going back to work for my sake.”

lines.japanese: 「ええ、自分のためにね」
lines.english: “Yes. For her own sake.”

lines.japanese: 「それはそうと、おまえ、優と仕事の話でもしてたのか？」
lines.english: “Setting that aside, were you discussing work with Yu?”
“Oh.”

lines.japanese: そうだった。まだ途中だったことを思いだした。
lines.english: Right. I remembered we had never finished.

lines.japanese: 「ふん。おい鷲介、やることが出来たんなら、こっちは気を使わなくていいからな」
lines.english: “Hm. Listen, Shusuke. If you've got something to do, don't worry about us here.”

lines.japanese: 「え？　なにがですか？」
lines.english: “What do you mean?”

lines.japanese: 「日野君と玉泉君のことなら、１２月に入ってから安定しているみたいだ。予定のある日は無理して出勤しなくていいぞ」
lines.english: “Hino and Tamaizumi seem to have settled into a stable rhythm since December began. If you've got plans, you don't need to force yourself to come in.”
“Oh. Right...”

lines.japanese: 俺はがしがしと後ろ頭を掻いた。最近休みがちだったし、あんまりマスターの手伝いをしてあげられなかったなあ。
lines.english: I scratched the back of my head. I’d been taking so much time off lately, I hadn’t done much to help the manager.

lines.japanese: 「まあ二人が関係を保てているのはおまえのお陰でもあるんだ。顔射するぞ」
lines.english: “Besides, you're one reason those two have maintained their relationship. I'm gonna come on your face.”

lines.japanese: 「はあ、でも俺なにもしてないですよ」
lines.english: “Maybe, but I haven't done anything.”

lines.japanese: 「いや玉泉君もだいぶ柔らかくなったと思うぞ。もちろん全てがおまえの影響だとは言わないがな」
lines.english: “No, I think Tamaizumi has softened considerably. I wouldn't claim that's entirely your influence, of course.”

lines.japanese: 「元々おまえのペースでとは言ったが、よくやってくれた。もちろんこれからも手伝ってもらえるなら、正月が過ぎるぐらいまでは歓迎するぞ」
lines.english: “I told you to work at your own pace, and you've done well. Naturally, if you want to continue helping, you're welcome through the New Year.”

lines.japanese: 「うわあ、残り二週間もない」
lines.english: “Wow. That's less than two weeks away.”

lines.japanese: 「ふーん、手が空いてるなら私から仕事を振ってあげられるかもよ。ま、その前に千歳君にはＰＣとケータイを持ってもらわないとね」
lines.english: “Hmm. If you have free time, I may be able to send more work your way. But first, Chitose, you'll need to get yourself a computer and a cell phone.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、実は両方手に入れたんです」
lines.english: “Actually, I got both.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ、ほんと？」
lines.english: “What? Really?”

lines.japanese: 俺は自分の携帯電話を差しだして米田さんに番号を見せた。彼女は一瞬驚いた表情を浮かべたが、すぐにいつもの笑顔へ戻って自分のケータイに登録してくれた。
lines.english: I held out my phone and showed Yoneda the number. Surprise crossed her face for an instant, but her usual smile quickly returned, and she added it to her phone.

lines.japanese: 「そっか。じゃあこれからはウェイターじゃなくてフリーライター千歳君に逆戻りだ」
lines.english: “I see. Then from now on, you go back to being Chitose the freelance writer instead of Chitose the waiter.”

lines.japanese: 「ふふふ、モテモテだな俺」
lines.english: “Heh-heh. I’m a popular guy.”

lines.japanese: 「千歳さん、１５分過ぎてます」
lines.english: “Chitose, your fifteen minutes are over.”

lines.japanese: 「うひい」
lines.english: “Eeegh.”

lines.japanese: 「ははは、本当にモテモテで羨ましいぞ、こいつぅ」
lines.english: “Hahaha. You really are popular. I'm jealous, you devil.”

lines.japanese: ふん、羨ましいだろ。バイト仲間に囲まれて楽しいもんね。
lines.english: Hmph. Jealous, aren't you? I was surrounded by my friends from work, and I was having fun.

lines.japanese: 今年中にもう一度来られるといいな、アレキサンダー。
lines.english: I hoped I could come to Alexander at least once more before the year ended.

lines.japanese: 「ただいまー……」
lines.english: “I'm home...”

lines.japanese: 玄関には俺の革靴とスニーカー。それに小鳩の小さな靴がいくつか。
lines.english: My dress shoes and sneakers stood in the entryway, along with several pairs of Kobato's little shoes.

lines.japanese: それに加えて人形の着せ替え用に作られたようなおもちゃみたいな靴がちょこんと揃えておいてある。持ちあげてみると俺の手も入らなそうだ。なんだこれ。
lines.english: And beside them sat a pair of toy-like shoes that looked made for dressing a doll. When I picked one up, it didn't look as though my hand would fit inside. What was this?

lines.japanese: 顔を上げると二つの駆け足が聞こえてきた。
lines.english: I raised my head at the sound of two sets of running feet.

lines.japanese: 「お兄ちゃん、おかえりー」
lines.english: “Welcome home, Big Brother!”

lines.japanese: 「ドラ、おかえり」
lines.english: “Welcome home, Dora.”

lines.japanese: 「あのなアリス、この場合『おかえり』じゃなくて『お邪魔してます』」
lines.english: “Listen, Alice. Guests don’t welcome the homeowner back. You’re supposed to say, ‘Thanks for having me over.’”

lines.japanese: まん丸な目で俺を見上げる四つの瞳。憎まれ口を叩いてはみたものの、悪い気はしなかった。
lines.english: Four round eyes looked up at me. I'd made a snide remark, but I didn't really mind.

lines.japanese: 「アリスちゃんは『おかえり』でいいのに。私も妹ができたみたいでうれしい」
lines.english: “Alice can say welcome home. I'm happy. It's like I have a little sister now.”

lines.japanese: 自分の妹に言われても賛同しかねる。
lines.english: Coming from my actual little sister, that was a sentiment I found difficult to endorse.

lines.japanese: 「ドラを待ってたのに、なかなか帰ってこない」
lines.english: “I was waiting for Dora, but you did not come home.”

lines.japanese: ぷーと頬を膨らませて俺の足をぺしと叩いた。これは抗議のつもりなんだろうか。
lines.english: She puffed out her cheeks and gave my leg a little smack. Was that supposed to be a protest?

lines.japanese: 「ああ待っててくれたのか。それはすまんかった。でも……」
lines.english: “Oh, you waited for me? Sorry about that. But...”

lines.japanese: 時計を見るともういい時間。
lines.english: I checked the clock. It was already rather late.

lines.japanese: 「これから帰るんだろうけど、時間の方は大丈夫なのか。それとも今日も一泊いっとく？」
lines.english: “You're going home now, right? Will you be all right this late? Or are you staying the night again?”

lines.japanese: 「いいえ、平気です。ちゃんとタクシー代をもらってきました」
lines.english: “No, I am fine. I was given taxi fare.”

lines.japanese: おちょこをくいっと傾ける俺を無視して、アリスはがま口の財布を取りだしてずいと差しだしてきた。ぱちん。ぱかっ。ブルジョワジー。
lines.english: Ignoring my pantomime of tilting back a sake cup, Alice produced a clasp purse and thrust it toward me. Snap. Open. Bourgeoisie.

lines.japanese: 「電話を借りてもいいですか」
lines.english: “May I use the telephone?”

lines.japanese: 「うん。かけ方分かる？」
lines.english: “Sure. Do you know how?”

lines.japanese: 「分からなければ聞きます」
lines.english: “If I do not know, I will ask.”

lines.japanese: アリスはぺったぺったと電話のところまで歩いていくと、いくつかのプッシュボタンを押して何かぼそぼそとしゃべっていた。結局小鳩が手招きされ、我が家の住所を受話器の向こうに伝えていた。
lines.english: Alice padded over to the telephone, pressed several buttons, and murmured something into the receiver. In the end she beckoned Kobato over, and Kobato gave the person on the other end our address.

lines.japanese: 「バイバイ、ドラ。小鳩、また明日」
lines.english: “Bye-bye, Dora. Kobato, see you tomorrow.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、またねー」
lines.english: “Okay. See you!”

lines.japanese: ドアの外まで見送ると、また遊んであげるわ坊やという意味の言葉を残して排気ガスの音と共に去っていった。ぎょっとした運転手が振りむいたときの顔が忘れられない。
lines.english: We saw her to the door. She left behind words that meant something like, I'll play with you again, little boy, then vanished to the sound of exhaust. I would never forget the driver's face as he spun around in alarm.

lines.japanese: 羽田家が二人住まいの静けさに包まれる。俺は玄関に戻りながら、思ったことを聞いてみた。
lines.english: The Haneda house settled into the quiet of a two-person household. As I returned to the entryway, I asked what had occurred to me.

lines.japanese: 「アリス、日本語うまくなってない？」
lines.english: “Is it just me, or is Alice getting better at Japanese?”

lines.japanese: 「うん、今日も学校終わってから一日、ま、まんつーまん？　だったから」
lines.english: “Yeah. We spent the whole day after school doing... m-man-to-man?”

lines.japanese: 小鳩は英語が下手だなと思ったけど、それはあえて口にしなかった（親切）。
lines.english: I thought Kobato's English needed work, but kindly chose not to mention it.

lines.japanese: なんか疲れたので布団に寝転がろうと思いながらふすまに手をかけた。
lines.english: I felt tired and reached for the sliding door, intending to lie down in bed.

lines.japanese: あ、そういえば最近こっちの部屋に入ってないな……。
lines.english: Oh. Come to think of it, I hadn't been in this room lately...

lines.japanese: すぐ横にあったので、なんとなく洋間の扉に手を移した。
lines.english: The other door was right beside it, so for no particular reason, I moved my hand to the Western-style room instead.

lines.japanese: しかしなんていうか……自分の部屋だけどセンスないよなあ。
lines.english: Still... This was my own room, but God, the decor was awful.

lines.japanese: 頭のどこかから抗議の声が聞こえてきたけど無視した。長々と解説が始まったけどそれも全て無視した。
lines.english: A voice protested somewhere inside my head. I ignored it. The voice launched into a long explanation. I ignored that too.

lines.japanese: 素晴らしい！　フローリングの部屋に一点癒しを添えるこの黄味がかったグリーンのチェアーといい普通には思いつかないアイドルのポスター！　一見無造作に見えてバランスの取れたこの配置！　マーベラス！
lines.english: Magnificent! Behold the yellow-green chair that brings one soothing note to the hardwood room! The idol poster no ordinary mind would think to display! A composition that appears casual at first glance, yet possesses exquisite balance! Marvelous!

lines.japanese: とうとう自分で自分を誉めはじめた。さすがに哀れになってきたがそれも全て無視した。
lines.english: He had finally begun praising himself. It was almost pitiful, but I ignored every word of that too.

lines.japanese: はっ、つかどう見てもセンスないだろこの部屋。なんだこのポスター、フリッキー５？　今では懐かしさを通りこして、笑いのジャンルとして成立するレベル……。
lines.english: Hah. However you looked at it, this room had no taste. And what was this poster? Fricky Five? It had gone beyond nostalgia by now. It qualified as a genre of comedy in its own right...

lines.japanese: 剥がしてやろうと手を伸ばしたら、昼の光景が頭をよぎった。あの時見た一瞬のフラッシュバック。フリッキー５のポスター。
lines.english: I reached up to tear it down, and the scene from that afternoon crossed my mind. The instant of memory I had glimpsed. The Fricky Five poster.

lines.japanese: 伸ばした手が自然とポスターに伸びていく。違う、このクソださいポスターを剥がそうってだけで、俺の意思で動かしてるんだ。
lines.english: My outstretched hand moved naturally toward the poster. No. I was only going to tear down this hideously tacky thing. I was moving my hand of my own free will.

lines.japanese: こんなだせえポスター……う、ううっ。
lines.english: This stupid, ugly poster... U-ugh.

lines.japanese: 「わあっ！」
lines.english: “Wah!”

lines.japanese: 部屋には俺しかいないのに、引いた手を胸に抱えてあとずさった。
lines.english: Though I was alone in the room, I snatched my hand back to my chest and retreated.

lines.japanese: なんだ、何をしようとしてたんだ今。俺は少し早い動悸を隠すように、この部屋から逃げだした。
lines.english: What had I just been about to do? I fled the room as if that could hide how hard my heart was pounding.

lines.japanese: 「あれ、お兄ちゃん。夕飯まだだよ。もうちょっと待っててね」
lines.english: “Oh, Big Brother. Dinner isn’t ready yet. Wait just a little longer.”

lines.japanese: 下りた一階では、小鳩が食事の準備をしていた。手に鍋を持って台所と居間を行き来している。
lines.english: Downstairs, Kobato was preparing the meal. Pot in hand, she moved back and forth between the kitchen and the living room.
“Oh. Okay...”

lines.japanese: 「おいしそうでしょ、きんぴらごぼうだよ。えへへ」
lines.english: “Smells good, doesn't it? It's sweet-and-savory braised burdock. Hee-hee.”

lines.japanese: 鍋からは美味しそうな香りが漂ってきた。子供の頃もテーブルの前に座りながら楽しみにしていたあの香り――。
lines.english: A delicious smell drifted from the pot. The same smell I had waited for so eagerly at the table when I was a child—

lines.japanese: 「なあ小鳩、それ誰から習って……」
lines.english: “Kobato, who taught you to make that...?”

lines.japanese: 「えっ？」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 「あれ？」
lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese: そうだ、誰が作ってくれたきんぴらを楽しみにしてたんだ。お母さん？
lines.english: That was right. Whose braised burdock had I looked forward to? Mom's?

lines.japanese: なんでだろう、お母さんの顔が思いだせない。俺はそこに代わりとして小鳩の顔を当てはめようとした。
lines.english: Why couldn't I remember my mother's face? I tried to fit Kobato's face into the empty space instead.

lines.japanese: どるんと体が震えて世界が赤く見えた。まずい、これはまずい。俺はすぐに現実へと意識を呼びもどした。
lines.english: My body gave a sickening lurch, and the world flashed red. Bad. This was bad. I immediately dragged my awareness back into the present.

lines.japanese: 小鳩が小さく首を傾げる。
lines.english: Kobato tilted her little head.

lines.japanese: 「なあ小鳩、二階の部屋にあるポスター……」
lines.english: “Kobato. That poster in the upstairs room...”

lines.japanese: 「えっ、剥がしたの？」
lines.english: “What? Did you take it down?”

lines.japanese: 「い、いや、剥がしたわけじゃないけど……いや、剥がせなくて……」
lines.english: “N-no. I didn't take it down... I couldn't.”

lines.japanese: 「なんだか頭の中に昔のことが次々に出てきて、急に怖くなったんだ」
lines.english: “Memories from long ago started coming back, one after another. All of a sudden, I got scared.”

lines.japanese: 「な、小鳩、俺は子供のころ……」
lines.english: “Kobato, when I was little...”

lines.japanese: 「ううん」
lines.english: “No.”

lines.japanese: 気持ちが焦る俺に比べて小鳩は落ちついていた。それは全て知っているからこその余裕だろうか。
lines.english: Kobato remained calm while panic gnawed at me. Was that the composure of someone who already knew everything?

lines.japanese: 「迷ってるうちは知らない方がいい」
lines.english: “As long as you're still unsure, it's better not to know.”

lines.japanese: でもその一言で俺も心を落ちつかせることが出来た。
lines.english: Yet those words were enough to settle me too.

lines.japanese: 「……そうかな」
lines.english: “...You think so?”

lines.japanese: 「うん、知りたくなったときに言ってくれればいい」
lines.english: “Yes. Tell me when you want to know.”

lines.japanese: 「思い出せると思うから」
lines.english: “Because I think you'll be able to remember.”
“Okay...”

lines.japanese: 俺の返事はまだ曖昧だった。だけど小鳩が夕食の支度を始めたので、俺はテレビのスイッチを入れた。
lines.english: My answer was still uncertain. But Kobato went back to preparing dinner, so I switched on the television.

lines.japanese: 画面の中はクリスマス一色で賑わっていた。女レポーターからアニメのキャラまでみんなサンタの帽子をかぶってる。何故か分からないけどみんな楽しそうだった。
lines.english: The screen was alive with Christmas. Everyone from the female reporter to the cartoon characters wore Santa hats. I couldn't have said why, but they all looked happy.

lines.japanese: あと４日でクリスマス・イヴかあ……。
lines.english: Four days until Christmas Eve...
